preconditions.description: The input is a string containing the full standard input text.

preconditions.expression: len(lines) >= 1 and lines[0].strip().isdigit() if (lines := stdin.strip().splitlines()) else False
preconditions.description: The first line of input contains a single integer T representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(s, str) and s.islower() and s.isalpha() for s in lines[1:] if lines := stdin.strip().splitlines())
preconditions.description: Each subsequent line contains a string S consisting only of lowercase English letters.
The number of test cases T is between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(s) <= 200000 for s in lines[1:] if lines := stdin.strip().splitlines())
preconditions.description: The length of each string S is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout.strip().splitlines()) == int(lines[0].strip()) if (lines := stdin.strip().splitlines()) else False
postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(out_lines[i] == str(sum(1 for k in range(len(s)) if (s[k:] + s[:k]) == (s[k:] + s[:k])[::-1])) for i, s in enumerate(test_strings)) if (lines := stdin.strip().splitlines()) and (test_strings := lines[1:]) and (out_lines := stdout.strip().splitlines()) else False
postconditions.description: For each test case string S, the output line contains the count of cyclic shifts of S that are palindromes. A cyclic shift by k is formed by moving the first k characters to the end, resulting in S[k:] + S[:k]. A string is palindromic if it equals its reverse.
